Orders and Shipping Policy
1 Application
Orders for physical goods are accepted for delivery to serviceable Singapore addresses, subject to the delivery option, charges and conditions confirmed at checkout. This Policy governs delivery services, shipping fees, changes to orders, tracking, partial deliveries and delivery problems. A request to change or cancel an order does not constitute confirmation that the change or cancellation has taken effect. All dates use Singapore time. Calendar days include weekends and public holidays. Business days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and Singapore public holidays. Delivery periods and service targets are estimates unless an express commitment has been confirmed for the order.

Orders and Shipping Policy
2.1 Available delivery services
The following doorstep delivery services may be available at checkout: (i) standard delivery, normally taking two (2) to five (5) business days after carrier pickup; and (ii) express delivery, normally taking one (1) to two (2) business days after carrier pickup. Availability depends on the delivery address and the goods purchased. The service applicable to an existing order is the service recorded for that order; the courier's name alone does not establish the service purchased. International delivery, lockers, collection points, installation and scheduled delivery appointments are not included in the standard offering. A request concerning a service not confirmed for the order requires review rather than an assumed entitlement.

Orders and Shipping Policy
2.2 Delivery periods and appointments
The estimated periods in section 2.1 begin when the carrier accepts the parcel, not when the order is placed, paid or assigned a label. Where the shipment has an updated estimated delivery date, that shipment-specific date takes precedence over a general service estimate. A specific arrival time cannot be reserved through the standard delivery service. The customer should arrange for an authorized recipient where necessary. An estimate does not guarantee delivery on a particular date, and an unsupported revised date must not be presented as confirmed.

Orders and Shipping Policy
2.3 Changes to the shipping option
A customer may request a service change before fulfillment begins under section 4.1. A change is subject to: (a) availability for the replacement service; (b) serviceability of the delivery address; (c) acceptance of any revised shipping charge; and (d) confirmation that the amendment has been recorded. Once fulfillment begins, a service upgrade or expedited handling is not guaranteed and requires human review. A request alone does not amend the purchased service.

Orders and Shipping Policy
3.1 Applicable charge
The shipping fee for a prospective purchase is the charge confirmed at checkout. For an existing purchase, the applicable fee is the amount recorded on that order, including any recorded discount and tax components. Historical charges are not recalculated using current catalog prices. A free-shipping threshold or loyalty benefit applies only where it formed part of the purchase terms. A customer disputing a shipping charge may submit the order reference and relevant payment information for review.

Orders and Shipping Policy
3.2 Separate parcels and additional charges
An order may be divided into several parcels without creating an additional shipping charge. The original fee must not be multiplied by the number of shipments or tracking numbers. A suspected duplicate charge is subject to payment review. Two pending authorizations do not necessarily represent two settled charges, and the same amount will not be refunded twice.

section_title: Shipping fees on cancellation or return
search_text:
Orders and Shipping Policy
3.3 Shipping fees on cancellation or return
For an accepted full cancellation before fulfillment, the refund calculation includes the original recorded shipping and tax components, subject to the captured balance and earlier refunds. For an accepted whole-order return due to store fault, the recorded outbound shipping fee is refundable once. For change-of-mind returns, the original outbound fee is normally retained. A partial return does not automatically make the whole outbound fee refundable. Delay alone does not establish an automatic entitlement to compensation or a shipping-fee refund. Disputed fees and missing allocations require review.

Orders and Shipping Policy
4.1 Changes before fulfillment
A cancellation, address correction or delivery-service change may be accepted while the order is processing and fulfillment has not begun. For this purpose, the ordinary change period ends when any of the following occurs: (i) a shipping label is generated; (ii) warehouse packing begins; (iii) any quantity is fulfilled; or (iv) the parcel is collected by the carrier. A processing status alone does not establish that the change period is still open. A label may exist before a pickup scan appears. Where the relevant status is unavailable or contradictory, the request requires human review.

Orders and Shipping Policy
4.2 Cancellation and refund
An eligible cancellation takes effect only when confirmation is issued and the order record is updated. The refundable amount following a full cancellation is the captured balance, including recorded original shipping and tax, less any amount already refunded or pending refund. An order that was not paid does not create a refund entitlement. A pending authorization may require release rather than repayment of settled funds. A cancellation confirmation does not establish that the payment has already been returned; refunds are returned to the original payment method. Initiation is targeted within two (2) business days after final approval and required checks, with an estimated five (5) to ten (10) business days for supported card and PayNow payments to appear after processing.

Orders and Shipping Policy
4.3 Requests after fulfillment begins
Cancellation or amendment after fulfillment begins is subject to human review and cannot be guaranteed. Once goods have been delivered, a request to send them back is a return request rather than a pre-dispatch cancellation. An already cancelled order must not be cancelled again. Any financial query concerning it remains subject to the original payment and refund history.

Orders and Shipping Policy
4.4 Delivery address corrections
Before fulfillment, a customer may request correction of the delivery address by providing the complete replacement Singapore address. The correction is subject to verification of the customer's authority, serviceability and confirmation of the amendment. After fulfillment begins, redirection is not guaranteed, including where a label exists but pickup has not occurred. A request will be referred for human review. The original address remains the recorded destination until an amendment is confirmed. An incorrect-address report does not automatically establish loss or store fault. Failed delivery follows section 7.3; a delivered-but-not-received claim follows section 7.4.

Orders and Shipping Policy
4.5 Additional products or quantities
Products cannot be added to a paid order and paid quantities cannot be increased through an ordinary amendment. Additional goods require a new order. If the customer wishes to cancel and reorder instead, the original order must independently satisfy section 4.1. Cancellation is not guaranteed merely because a new order is intended.

Orders and Shipping Policy
5.1 Order and parcel status
An order may be processing, shipped, partially fulfilled, delivered or cancelled. These statuses describe different stages and must be considered together with the associated shipment records. In particular: (a) processing does not necessarily mean warehouse work has not begun; (b) a shipping label does not establish carrier pickup; (c) delivery of one parcel does not establish delivery of all items; and (d) several tracking numbers do not necessarily indicate duplicate orders. Order references, shipment references and carrier tracking numbers identify different records. Customer-specific order, address and payment information is available only after the customer's authority to access the order has been established; possession of an order reference alone is insufficient.

Orders and Shipping Policy
5.2 Missing or invalid tracking information
A missing scan or invalid tracking number may reflect an unupdated record, an incorrect reference or a carrier-system issue. It does not, by itself, establish cancellation or loss. The latest confirmed shipping event and any discrepancy should be used when enquiring about progress. An update, carrier contact or expedited handling must not be presented as completed unless it has been confirmed.

Orders and Shipping Policy
5.3 Estimated delivery date
The latest estimated date recorded for the affected shipment is the applicable estimate. If no shipment-specific date exists, a general period under section 2.1 may be given only where the service and pickup date are established. An estimated date is not proof that delivery occurred. Missing dates and conflicting status information require clarification or review, not substitution of an assumed arrival date.

Orders and Shipping Policy
6.1 Orders containing several parcels
Goods from one order may be dispatched separately, with different shipment references, tracking numbers and arrival dates. The order remains a single purchase unless the transaction records show otherwise. Each parcel's progress is assessed separately. A parcel delivered before the others does not establish that the remaining quantities are missing. Splitting the order does not create a further delivery charge under section 3.2.

Orders and Shipping Policy
6.2 Missing items and outstanding parcels
Where only part of an order has arrived, the goods expected in each parcel must be considered. If an absent item is allocated to an outstanding parcel, the delivery provisions in section 7 apply to that parcel. If the item should have been inside a delivered parcel, the customer may raise an incomplete-delivery claim for the affected quantities. Where the allocation or contents are disputed or cannot be established, the matter requires clarification or human review.

Orders and Shipping Policy
6.3 Return dates and affected quantities
For separate deliveries, each item's return period begins when the parcel containing that item is delivered. The earliest delivery in the order does not determine the deadline for every item. A return or refund concerns only the accepted affected quantities. Retained goods, outstanding parcels and unrelated items do not become refundable solely because another item is returned. Any refund is based on the amount paid for the affected quantities, including recorded discount and tax allocations, less amounts already refunded or pending refund.

Orders and Shipping Policy
7.1 Delayed deliveries
A parcel is delayed if it has not arrived after the latest recorded estimated delivery date. A missing or late scan alone is not confirmation of loss. Where the parcel remains undelivered more than three (3) calendar days after that estimate, the case will be referred for human investigation. A customer may request human assistance sooner. If no reliable estimate exists, the matter requires review rather than an invented waiting-period end date. The ordinary waiting period does not apply to confirmed loss or transit damage under section 7.2, or to a delivered-but-not-received claim under section 7.4.

Orders and Shipping Policy
7.2 Confirmed loss or transit damage
Notwithstanding the ordinary waiting period in section 7.1, a carrier declaration of loss or damage in transit requires immediate human review. The affected parcels and quantities, and any existing claim, will be considered. A customer allegation alone does not constitute a carrier declaration. Confirmed non-delivery may support a refund without physical return following human review. Opening an investigation does not itself approve a refund or replacement.

section_title: Failed delivery and return to sender
search_text:
Orders and Shipping Policy
7.3 Failed delivery and return to sender
An unsuccessful attempt is subject to the recorded reason and the carrier's confirmed redelivery or collection arrangement. Another attempt, appointment or collection deadline is not guaranteed unless confirmed. Where the parcel is returning to sender, the outcome and any refund are subject to review of the reason and the parcel's disposition. An unavailable recipient or an incorrect address does not automatically establish store fault. Shipping-fee treatment depends on the accepted resolution.

Orders and Shipping Policy
7.4 Delivered but not received
Where tracking shows delivery but the customer denies receipt, the claim will be referred for human investigation immediately. The ordinary waiting period in section 7.1 does not apply. Relevant circumstances may include: (i) whether a household member or authorized recipient accepted the parcel; (ii) the recorded delivery location and time; (iii) any delivery photograph, signature or safe-place confirmation; and (iv) whether the confirmation concerns the correct parcel and address. A delivery scan or the existence of a photograph alone is not conclusive proof of correct receipt. The customer is not required to carry out an unsafe search. Unverified or conflicting evidence remains subject to human review.

Orders and Shipping Policy
7.5 Outcome of delivery investigation
A confirmed finding of non-delivery may support a refund for the affected goods. The amount is limited to the amount paid for those goods and any approved shipping and tax components, less amounts already refunded or pending refund. Where delivery is confirmed or remains disputed, the customer may seek review of the decision and relevant evidence. An investigation, accepted resolution and completed payment are separate events. A refund, reshipment, carrier contact or address amendment must not be treated as completed solely because it was requested or accepted for review.

Returns and Refunds Policy
1 Application for returns and refunds
Subject to the conditions in this Policy, customers may apply for the return of purchased goods and/or a refund. A request may concern goods received by the customer or goods that have not been received. Submission of a request does not, by itself, constitute acceptance of the return or approval of a refund. This Policy applies to physical goods purchased in Singapore dollars for delivery within Singapore. The same standard conditions apply to all customer loyalty tiers. All dates are assessed in Singapore time. Calendar days include weekends and public holidays. Where a period is stated in business days, Saturdays, Sundays and Singapore public holidays are excluded. A specific exception changes only the condition expressly identified; the remaining conditions continue to apply.

Returns and Refunds Policy
2.1 Goods received by the customer
A customer may submit a return request within thirty (30) calendar days after delivery of the affected goods. The delivery date is day zero, and a request submitted on the thirtieth day is within the ordinary request period. The period runs from actual delivery, not the order date, payment date or dispatch date. Where an order is delivered in separate parcels, each affected item's period runs from delivery of the parcel containing that item. Delivery of another parcel from the same order does not shorten the period. If an item's delivery date or parcel allocation cannot be established, the request will require clarification or human review. The date the request was first recorded determines whether it was submitted on time. A timely request does not become late because inspection or review takes place later. However, timely submission does not waive the conditions relating to evidence, item condition or return shipment. For example, goods delivered on 5 October have an ordinary request deadline of 4 November, inclusive. Requests outside the ordinary return period are addressed in section 2.6.

section_title: Goods not received by the customer
search_text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.2 Goods not received by the customer
A customer may raise a non-receipt claim where: (i) the estimated delivery date has passed and the parcel has not arrived; (ii) tracking shows delivery but the customer has not received the parcel; or (iii) the carrier has confirmed that the parcel was lost or damaged in transit. Non-receipt claims require investigation of the shipment status, delivery records and any carrier findings. A non-receipt claim does not require the customer to return goods that they do not possess. A refund remains subject to the investigation outcome and the conditions in section 6 of this Policy.

Returns and Refunds Policy
2.3 Reasons for a return request
A return and/or refund may be requested in the following circumstances: (a) the parcel is empty or the quantity received is less than the quantity purchased; (b) supplied accessories or components are missing; (c) the goods differ from the purchased item or variant, such as a different model, size or colour; (d) the goods are defective or do not function as intended; (e) the goods sustained physical damage before or during delivery; or (f) the customer wishes to return goods in their original, unused condition due to a change of mind. The reason selected must correspond to the issue reported. A concern that goods may be counterfeit is subject to human review under section 7.3 rather than an automatic refund or rejection. Before goods are treated as missing, any outstanding parcels from the same order must be taken into account.

Returns and Refunds Policy
2.4 Change-of-mind returns
A change-of-mind return is available within the period in section 2.1 only where the goods: (i) are unused and in their original condition; (ii) remain in their original packaging; (iii) retain original tags or labels, where supplied; (iv) include all accessories, components and gifts supplied with the purchase; and (v) were not designated final sale at the time of purchase. The affected goods and quantities must be identified in the request. Goods returned as part of an approved bundle must include the components specified in that return authorization. A change in preference is not treated as a defect where the goods match the purchased specification. The conditions for damaged, faulty or incorrect goods, including exceptions to final-sale and original-packaging requirements, are set out in section 2.5.

section_title: Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
search_text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
2.5 Final-sale goods and the store-fault exception
Goods marked final sale at the time of purchase are excluded from change-of-mind returns. A product's general category or a label added after purchase does not establish that it was sold as final sale. Notwithstanding that exclusion, a request concerning verified arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item may be accepted within the period in section 2.1. In those circumstances, the unused and original-packaging conditions may be waived where opening, testing or loss of packaging was reasonably connected with discovering or reporting the fault. Secure return packaging is still required where the goods are to be returned. This exception does not cover damage caused by later misuse, extend the thirty-day request period or establish an entitlement to a refund without assessment. Evidence and any required inspection remain applicable. Missing original packaging alone is not a sufficient reason to reject a qualifying damaged-item claim.

Returns and Refunds Policy
2.6 Requests outside the ordinary conditions
A request submitted after thirty days will be referred for human review of the stated circumstances. It is not automatically accepted or rejected. Any approved exception must identify the goods and the condition or deadline being varied. Contact with customer service or an unanswered earlier message does not, by itself, establish an approved extension. Digital goods, services and standalone promotional gifts are outside the standard physical-return process. A claim concerning such a purchase requires human review; absence of a physical-return process does not automatically determine whether a separate refund claim is valid.

Returns and Refunds Policy
3.1 Evidence relevant to the request
Customers should provide the order reference, affected goods and quantities, a description of the issue and relevant supporting evidence. Depending on the reason, this may include: (a) photographs of visible damage, the goods and their packaging; (b) photographs of the goods received and their identifying labels where an incorrect item is alleged; (c) photographs or packing information showing the contents of an incomplete parcel; or (d) a description and, where safe and practical, a demonstration of a malfunction. Customers must not operate unsafe goods to demonstrate a defect. Non-receipt is assessed using shipment and investigation evidence rather than a photograph of goods that are absent. Passwords, full payment-card details and unrelated personal information are not required. Where evidence cannot be provided, accessed or safely obtained, the exception in section 3.2 applies.

Returns and Refunds Policy
3.2 Unavailable, inaccessible or unsafe evidence
If evidence is unavailable, inaccessible or unsafe to produce, the limitation must be recorded and the request referred for human review instead of automatic rejection. This is an exception to the ordinary evidence requirements in section 3.1. An uploaded attachment is not automatically accepted as verified evidence. A human reviewer will determine whether the available material is sufficient. Referral for review does not itself approve the return or refund.

Returns and Refunds Policy
3.3 Clarification and existing requests
Further relevant information may be requested where the issue, delivery date, quantities or condition remains unclear. Customer statements, inspection findings and confirmed transaction details will be considered separately; a disputed statement is not treated as an established fact merely because it appears in a request. Additional evidence concerning an existing case should be attached to that case. Repeated submissions for the same goods do not create separate refund entitlements. Any earlier approval remains limited to the goods, quantities and resolution it expressly covered.

Returns and Refunds Policy
4.1 Return authorization
Goods must not be dispatched until a return authorization and return destination have been provided. The authorization identifies the goods, quantities and approved shipping arrangement. Permission to send goods back is not confirmation that inspection has passed or a refund has been processed.

Returns and Refunds Policy
4.2 Dispatch deadline
Authorized goods must be handed to the carrier within seven (7) calendar days after approval of the return, unless an extension under section 4.5 applies. The approval date is day zero and the seventh day is included. Carrier acceptance or a drop-off receipt establishes dispatch. Creation of a label alone does not establish that the goods were sent. The dispatch deadline concerns handover, not arrival at the warehouse; delivery to the warehouse after that deadline does not necessarily mean dispatch was late.

Returns and Refunds Policy
4.3 Shipping arrangements and amendments
The return may use an authorized pickup, prepaid label or customer-arranged shipment, as specified for the case. A customer-arranged shipment is reimbursable only under the conditions in section 5.1. Changes to the method, collection date or return details may be requested before carrier handover and take effect only when confirmed. Once the goods have been handed over, changes are subject to the carrier's handling and are not guaranteed. A pickup or label must not be treated as arranged until confirmation has been issued.

Returns and Refunds Policy
4.4 Condition and packaging
Goods must be packed securely to prevent damage or loss during return. The return must include the authorized quantities and the accessories, components and gifts required by the approved resolution. The customer should retain the return reference and proof of handover. Original packaging remains required for a change-of-mind return. Where section 2.5 applies and original packaging is damaged or unavailable, suitable protective packaging may be used instead. A claim concerning an original fault must not be rejected solely because the original packaging is absent.

Returns and Refunds Policy
4.5 Extensions and failed collection
A recorded human-approved extension replaces the ordinary dispatch deadline only for the named return and the new date specified. A failed store-arranged pickup may support a request for an extension but does not create one automatically. Late or unverified dispatch requires human review. A customer must not be told that the return was automatically cancelled without a recorded cancellation or decision.

Returns and Refunds Policy
4.6 Unsafe returns
Leaking goods, unsafe batteries and other goods presenting a handling risk require human review and specific return instructions. Customers should not dispatch such goods using an ordinary return arrangement or dispose of them unless expressly instructed to do so.

Returns and Refunds Policy
5.1 Cost of return shipment
For a verified store-fault return, the store bears the approved return-shipping cost using the authorized arrangement. Where the customer arranges shipment, reimbursement requires: (i) prior approval of the method and cost; and (ii) evidence of the amount actually paid. For a change-of-mind return, return shipping is normally the customer's responsibility. The applicable charge or responsibility must be explained before handover. Unconfirmed fault or disputed charges require further review before reimbursement is agreed.

Returns and Refunds Policy
5.2 Original outbound shipping
The original outbound shipping fee is normally not refunded for a change-of-mind return. Where an approved store-fault resolution affects the whole order, the recorded outbound fee is included once. For a partial return, any outbound-fee refund depends on a recorded allocation or an expressly approved amount. The whole fee is not automatically refundable for each returned item. For an accepted full cancellation before fulfillment, the refund includes the recorded original shipping and tax, less amounts already refunded or pending refund.

Returns and Refunds Policy
6.1 Conditions for payment
A refund is issued after the request has been accepted and, where a physical return is required, the returned goods have been received and the applicable inspection completed. The inspection considers the identity, quantities, completeness and conditions relevant to the original return reason, including any exception in section 2.5. The store targets inspection within three (3) business days after warehouse receipt. Return tracking marked delivered does not itself establish that inspection is complete. A delay or a disputed finding may be raised for review under section 7. Physical return may be waived following human review where non-delivery is confirmed or return is unsafe or impractical. The waiver applies only to the goods and resolution specified. It does not remove the requirement to establish the payment and refundable amount.

Returns and Refunds Policy
6.2 Refund amount
The amount is based on the approved affected quantities and the amount paid for those goods, including the applicable recorded discount and tax allocations. It is not calculated using a later catalog price. Shipping components for returns are governed by section 5 of this Policy. For an accepted full cancellation before fulfillment, the recorded original shipping and tax are included, subject to the captured balance and earlier refunds. A partial return does not entitle the customer to reimbursement of retained or unaffected goods. Where the value of an accessory, a discount allocation or another component cannot be established, the amount requires review rather than an assumed allocation.

Returns and Refunds Policy
6.3 Payment destination and previous refunds
Refunds are made in SGD to the original payment method. They cannot be redirected to a different account or payment instrument supplied during a support conversation. The total of completed and pending refunds must not exceed the amount captured for the order. Amounts already refunded or reserved for an existing refund will be deducted from the remaining balance. Failed payments and uncaptured authorizations cannot be refunded as settled payments. Approval of a return does not authorize a duplicate refund.

Returns and Refunds Policy
6.4 Refund timeframe
The store targets refund initiation within two (2) business days after final acceptance and completion of the required receipt and inspection, or an approved waiver. Return authorization alone does not start this period. After processing, supported card and PayNow refunds normally appear within five (5) to ten (10) business days. These are estimated periods rather than guaranteed posting dates. Requested, accepted and pending refunds may not yet have been processed.

Returns and Refunds Policy
6.5 Delayed refunds and other resolutions
Where the relevant period has passed or the recorded status conflicts with the payment received, the customer may request further review. An additional refund will not be issued solely because an earlier refund is not yet visible. Exchange, replacement, repair, store credit and goodwill compensation require separate agreement. A request for one of these alternatives does not guarantee stock, dispatch or payment.

Returns and Refunds Policy
7.1 Grounds for a dispute
A dispute may be raised concerning: (a) a return parcel reported as not received; (b) missing goods, quantities, accessories or bundle components; (c) a different item in the returned parcel; (d) damage, a fault or a condition inconsistent with the accepted return reason; (e) the authenticity of purchased or returned goods; or (f) whether a change-of-mind return meets the applicable condition requirements. A dispute initiates a review. It does not establish that either party's account is correct or create a second refund entitlement.

section_title: Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
search_text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.2 Incomplete, damaged, faulty or wrong goods
The original return reason, purchase details, supporting evidence and inspection findings will be considered together. Review must distinguish the original reported fault from an allegation of additional damage, missing contents or a different item during the return. The customer is not automatically responsible for damage merely because the goods were returned damaged. A qualifying original fault remains subject to section 2.5. Conflicting accounts or inspection findings will be referred for human review rather than automatic refund or rejection.

Returns and Refunds Policy
7.3 Counterfeit products
A claim concerning authenticity will be referred for human review. Relevant product, packaging and purchase evidence may be requested. A brand name, low price, image or allegation alone does not establish that goods are genuine or counterfeit. Any accepted resolution will identify the affected goods, whether physical return is required and the applicable refund. No special compensation or determination of authenticity is implied merely by raising the claim.

section_title: Goods returned due to change of mind
search_text:
Returns and Refunds Policy
7.4 Goods returned due to change of mind
A dispute may arise where inspection reports use, missing original packaging or tags, missing accessories, an incomplete bundle or a different item. The applicable conditions are those in section 2.4 and the agreed return authorization. If the customer contests the finding, the request will be referred for human review. Where the original reason concerns arrival damage, a defect or an incorrect item, section 2.5 must be considered rather than applying change-of-mind conditions without that exception.

Returns and Refunds Policy
7.5 Review and communication
The store may request further relevant evidence and will communicate the reviewed outcome and its reason. An unresolved allegation is not proof of misuse, fraud or ineligibility. Unavailable or unsafe evidence is handled under section 3.2. A customer may request human review of a disputed decision. Existing case details and additional evidence should remain associated with the same request. Contact with support is not, by itself, confirmation that an investigation, amendment or payment has been completed.
